newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rabin's dressing-gown still hangs in widow's home.
newsitem.headline: Rabin's dressing-gown still hangs in widow's home.

text.p: Yitzhak Rabin's dressing-gown still hangs in his bathroom just as it did the day the Israeli premier was assassinated a year ago, his widow Leah told the German weekly news magazine Der Spiegel.
Israel last Thursday marked the Jewish calendar anniversary of Rabin's assassination on November 4, 1995, by a right-wing Jew opposed to his peace policies with the Palestinians.
"I still have conversations with my husband," Leah Rabin told the magazine in an interview released in advance of Monday's edition.
"Not a single thing in our apartment has been changed. His desk is untouched, his dressing gown still hangs in the bathroom as it always did, the wardrobes haven't been touched."

Rabin's widow, who has bitterly criticised the policies of the hardline Likud government which came to power earlier this year, said she shared much of her grief with their granddaughter who moved the world with a tearful speech at Rabin's funeral.
"Noa has slept with me almost every night since then. We help each other," she said, in comments published in German.
"How pleased, how proud Yitzhak would have been if he had seen her complete her army officer's training course the week before last. We miss him every day, every hour."
Leah Rabin said Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat had taken the trouble to send her good wishes for the Jewish New Year.

"I keep hearing how Arafat calls my husband his brother. It's an amazing thing that we can make peace with a man whom we considered for a long time to be a terrorist. Today he comes through my door and I see him as part of my family," she said.
"I believe politicians like Arafat and King Hussein of Jordan sincerely regret my husband's death and miss him painfully. That's something you can't say of the current prime minister of Israel."
